blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: The number of paper submissions to major AI conferences has increased dramatically in recent years, substantially increasing the peer-review workload of researchers. At the same time, large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support peer review, both by individual reviewers and by conference organizations. While LLM capabilities have improved considerably, their evaluations may be influenced by linguistic characteristics that are unrelated to scientific content. In this work, we introduce a controlled experimental framework for studying such effects by systematically perturbing the linguistic style of research papers. Specifically, we rewrite papers to exhibit (i) linguistic features associated with native or non-native English writing, and (ii) high- or low-confidence linguistic features. To construct these interventions, we derive fine-grained rewriting instructions grounded in the linguistic literature and apply them using LLMs. Crucially, our interventions are designed to preserve the underlying scientific content. We then evaluate the resulting papers using different LLM reviewers. Our experiments expose a critical vulnerability in LLM-based peer review: reviewers systematically reward confident rhetoric independent of scientific content, raising serious concerns about the robustness of their assessments.
blocks.zh: 近年来,向大赦国际主要会议提交的文件数量急剧增加,大大增加了研究人员的同行审查工作量。 同时,大型语文模式越来越多地被个别审查人员和会议组织用于支持同行审查。 虽然LLM能力已大大提高,但其评价可能受与科学内容无关的语言特征的影响. 在这部作品中,我们引入了一个有控制的实验框架,通过系统干扰研究论文的语言风格来研究这种效果. 具体地说,我们改写了论文,以展示(一) 与本土或非本土英语写作相关的语言特征,(二) 高或低自信语言特征. 为了构建这些干预,我们从语言文献中得出了精细的重写指令,并使用LLMs加以应用. 关键的是,我们的干预旨在保护基本的科学内容。 然后,我们用不同的LLM审查员来评价由此产生的论文。 我们的实验暴露了基于LLM的同级审评中的一个关键弱点:审查者系统地奖励独立于科学内容的自信言论,使人们对其评估的稳健性表示严重关切。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
The peer-review process is an integral part of scientific publishing, but also requires substantial time and effort from researchers.
This challenge has become increasingly pronounced with the growing number of submissions to major AI conferences.
In parallel, recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have opened up new opportunities to automate or support parts of the reviewing process ( Jin et al., 2024 ; Lin et al., 2025 ; Dycke and Gurevych, 2026 ) .
Individual reviewers use LLMs to assist with the review process, while LLMs are also increasingly seen as systematic tools for generating or supporting peer review ( Demetrio et al., 2025 ; Baumann et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh:
同行审查进程是科学出版的一个组成部分,但也需要研究人员投入大量的时间和精力。
随着向大赦国际主要会议提交的材料越来越多,这一挑战已日益突出。
与此同时,最近大语言模型(LLMs)的进步为审查过程的自动化或部分支持开辟了新的机会(Jin等,2024;Lin等,2025;Dycke和Gurevich,2026.).
个别审查人员利用LLMs协助审评进程,而LLMs也日益被视为产生或支持同行审评的系统工具(Demetrio等,2025;Baumann等,2026)。

blocks.en:
However, the use of LLMs for peer review also introduces new risks.
LLM judgments can be influenced by properties that are unrelated to the actual quality of the evaluated content.
Prior work on LLM-as-a-judge has, for example, demonstrated biases related to the position of an answer or preferences towards outputs of the same LLM family ( Liu et al., 2024 ; Wataoka et al., 2024 ; Ye et al., 2025 ) .
Similar concerns have been identified specifically for LLM-based peer review as well.
LLM reviewers can be susceptible to adversarial modifications of papers ( Lin et al., 2025 ) , fail to reliably identify faulty scientific reasoning ( Dycke and Gurevych, 2026 ) , and exhibit biases based on author-related information such as affiliation, seniority, or publication history ( Vasu et al., 2026 ) .
Moreover, recent results suggest that even paraphrasing or stylistic properties of a paper can substantially affect LLM-generated review scores ( Kaneko, 2026 ; Kousha and Thelwall, 2026 ; Baumann et al., 2026 ) .
These findings raise the central question of our paper:
” How do we systematically measure whether LLM reviewers judge the research quality, rather than the linguistic style with which the research content is presented? ”
blocks.zh:
然而,将有限责任方案用于同行审查也带来了新的风险。
LLM判断可能受到与被评价内容的实际质量无关的属性的影响.
例如,以前关于LLM-as-a-judge的工作表明,对同一LLM家族产出的答复或偏好立场存在偏见(Liu等,2024;Wataoka等,2024;Ye等,2025)。
也特别为基于LLM的同行审评确定了类似的关切。
LLM审查员可能会受到论文的对抗性修改(Lin等,2025年),无法可靠地识别出错误的科学推理(Dycke和Gurevych,2026年),并基于作者相关信息表现出偏见,如归属,资历,或出版史(Vasu等,2026年).
此外,最近的结果表明,即使一纸的比喻性或结构性也会对LLM产生的审查分数产生重大影响(Kaneko,2026;Kousha和Thelwall,2026;Baumann等,2026)。
这些结论提出了我们文件的中心问题:
“ 我们如何系统地衡量LLM审查者是否判断研究质量,而不是研究内容呈现的语言风格? “

blocks.en:
In this work, we specifically study the impact of linguistic style on LLM-based peer review.
Researchers have different linguistic backgrounds, and previous work has already found evidence that language proficiency and writing style can influence human peer review ( Politzer-Ahles et al., 2020 ; Saposnik et al., 2014 ; Lee et al., 2006 ; Sayegh et al., 2024 ) .
Motivated by these human studies,
we focus on two complementary dimensions that together signal epistemic authority :
(i) the language proficiency reflected in the writing, and
(ii) the confidence with which the research is presented.
Language proficiency can signal author credibility ( Lev-Ari and Keysar, 2010 ) , while confident linguistic framing can influence the perceived scientific credibility ( Teigen, 2023 ) .
Both dimensions are
well characterized in the linguistic literature ( Hinkel, 2002 ; Hyland, 1996 ) ,
and should not substantially affect the assessment of the underlying research
quality.
blocks.zh:
在这部作品中,我们专门研究了语言风格对基于LLM的同行评审的影响.
研究人员有着不同的语言背景,而之前的作品已经发现了语言熟练度和写作风格可以影响人类同行评审的证据(Politzer-Ahles等,2020;Saposnik等,2014;Lee等,2006;Sayegh等,2024).

(一) 书写中反映的语言熟练程度,以及
(二) 研究所表现的信心。
语言熟练度可以表示作者的可信度(Lev-Ari和Keysar,2010年),而自信的语言框架可以影响感知的科学可信度(Teigen,2023年).

blocks.en:
Systematically studying such effects is challenging, as naturally occurring papers with different linguistic styles also differ in their research content and quality.
We therefore propose a controlled framework for perturbing a research paper along a specific linguistic dimension, while preserving its underlying research content.
Specifically, we rewrite papers to exhibit (i)  linguistic characteristics associated with native or non-native English writing, and (ii) high-confidence - or low-confidence linguistic characteristics.
Rather than relying on generic rewriting instructions, we derive fine-grained prompts from the linguistic literature to systematically control the corresponding stylistic features.
Crucially, we design these interventions to avoid distorting the content and thus the research quality of the paper, and verify the content integrity of the resulting rewrites.
To assess whether rewrites exhibit the intended stylistic characteristics
we use established linguistic measures.
The different rewrites are then given
to LLM reviewers, that provide us with a full-fledged peer review.
While review scores are the immediate quality signal, the arguments raised in reviews play an important role in the final decision process as well ( Arous et al., 2026 ) .
To this end, we integrate an automated annotation procedure for identifying positive and negative aspects in reviews ( Lu et al., 2025 ) .

因此,我们提议建立一个控制框架,以在保留其基本研究内容的同时,根据特定语言层面干扰一份研究文件。
具体而言,我们改写论文,以展示(一) 与本土或非本土英语写作有关的语言特征,(二) 高自信-或低自信语言特征。
我们不是依赖通用重写指示,而是从语言文献中得出了精细的提示来系统控制相应的文体特征.
重要的是,我们设计这些干预措施是为了避免扭曲文件的内容,从而扭曲其研究质量,并核实由此产生的重写内容的完整性。
评估重写是否显示出预定的风格特征

给LLM审查员, 为我们提供了一个全面的同行评审。
虽然评分是即刻的质量信号,但评分中提出的论据在最后决定过程中也发挥着重要作用(Arous等人,2026年)。
为此,我们将自动说明程序纳入审查中确定积极和消极方面(Lu等人,2025年)。

blocks.en:
While related work has used counterfactual modifications to study reasoning capabilities ( Dycke and Gurevych, 2026 ) , author-related biases ( Vasu et al., 2026 ) , or the general susceptibility of LLM reviewers to rewriting and paraphrasing ( Kaneko, 2026 ; Baumann et al., 2026 ) , framework isolates linguistic cues of epistemic authority and examines their effects on review scores and qualitative arguments.
We use this framework to study different state-of-the-art LLM reviewers and investigate whether their reviews systematically favor perceived language proficiency and confidence.
blocks.zh:
虽然相关工作使用反事实修改来研究推理能力(Dycke and Gurevych, 2026),与作者相关的偏差(Vasu等, 2026),或LLM审查员对重写和抛写的一般易感性(Kaneko, 2026;Baumann等, 2026),框架隔离了感知权威的语言提示并审查了其对复核分数和定性论证的影响.
我们利用这一框架来研究各种最新水平的LLM审评员,并调查他们的审评是否系统地有利于人们所认为的语言熟练程度和信心。

blocks.en:
Our experiments reveal that the two linguistic dimensions affect LLM reviewers differently. Across models, expressed confidence has a strong and consistent effect on evaluation even though the underlying scientific content remains unchanged.
In contrast, differences between native - and non-native associated writing are substantially smaller and more model-dependent.
More importantly, our controlled rewriting framework provides a practical way to stress-test LLM reviewers by varying specific linguistic cues and measuring when these changes alter review outcomes.
Our analysis further shows that these effects extend beyond review scores: LLM reviewers raise substantially different arguments across rewrites, focusing on different aspects of the paper and expressing different sentiments toward them.
blocks.zh:
我们的实验表明,两种语言维度对LLM审查者的影响不同. 在整个模型中,尽管基本科学内容保持不变,但表达的信心对评价具有强大而一致的影响。
相比之下,本地-非本地关联的书写方式差别要小得多,更依赖模型.
更重要的是,我们控制下的改写框架为压力测试LLM审评员提供了一个实用的方法,通过不同的特定语言提示并衡量这些变化何时改变审评结果。
我们的分析还表明,这些影响超出了审查分数: LLM审查员在改写过程中提出了截然不同的论点,侧重于论文的不同方面,并对论文表达不同的看法。

blocks.en: In summary, our main contributions are: ∙ \bullet We devise a controlled experimental framework for stress-testing LLM reviewers. By rewriting research papers along different linguistic dimensions in a content-preserving manner, our framework enables the systematic investigation of linguistic biases in LLM-based peer review. ∙ \bullet We design literature-grounded rewriting prompts to manipulate language proficiency and expressed confidence, and validate the resulting rewrites using established linguistic measures. ∙ \bullet We conduct experiments across state-of-the-art LLM reviewers. Our results reveal that expressed confidence has a strong and consistent effect on reviewer preferences, while effects associated with language proficiency are substantially smaller and vary across models.

blocks.en: 2 Methodology
blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en:
In this section, we introduce our experimental framework for
controlled linguistic interventions to detect stylistic biases in LLM reviewers.
Starting with the original paper, our framework proceeds in three stages.
First, we generate two versions that differ along a specific linguistic dimension, while preserving the underlying research content.
We then validate the content integrity of rewrites, and verify the presence of the respective linguistic style.
Finally, we provide the resulting versions to LLM reviewers and compare their reviews.
Figure 1 provides an overview of our framework.
blocks.zh:
在本节中,我们介绍我们的实验框架。
控制语言干预,以发现在LLM审查中存在的语气偏差。
从原始文件开始,我们的框架分三个阶段进行。
首先,我们产生两个不同语言层面的版本,同时保留基本的研究内容。
然后验证重写的内容完整性,并验证相应语言风格的存在.
最后,我们向LLM审查员提供由此产生的版本,并比较他们的审查。
图1概述了我们的框架。

blocks.en: 2.1 Linguistic Rewriting
blocks.zh: 2.1 语言改写

blocks.en:
A central challenge in designing the rewriting interventions is to obtain
linguistically distinguishable versions while changing only their linguistic realization and not the scientific content.
This challenge was also highlighted in prior work on linguistically informed LLM-rewriting ( Kunilovskaya et al., 2024 ) .
A simple solution would be to directly ask an LLM to imitate a particular linguistic style. However, this could surface stereotypical characteristics ( Cheng et al., 2023 ) or perturb the scientific content itself, leading to incomparable rewrites.
Hence,
we opt for a more principled approach and carefully design
rewriting prompts based on specific linguistic properties described in the corresponding literature.
blocks.zh:
设计重写干预措施的主要挑战是获得
在语言上可以区分的版本,同时只改变其语言上的实现,而不是科学的内容.
在以往关于语言上知情的LLM-改写的工作中也强调了这一挑战(Kunilovskaya等,2024年)。
一个简单的解决方案是直接要求LLM来模仿特定的语言风格. 然而,这可能暴露出陈规定型的特征(Cheng等人,2023年),或干扰科学内容本身,导致不可比拟的重写.
因此,
我们选择了更原则性的方法,并仔细设计
基于相应文献所描述的特定语言属性来重写提示.

blocks.en:
Preserving content integrity .
A crucial requirement of our interventions is that the scientific content, and thus the research quality of the paper, is preserved.
To this end, we design a set of content integrity rules shared across rewriting prompts (Figures 8 - 11 ). These rules specify which content must remain unchanged and require preserving the length and structure of the original text.
At the same time, all rewrites must remain grammatical and plausible as
professional
academic English, to avoid actually degrading the scientific quality by introducing grammatical mistakes or typos.

我们发言的一项关键要求是,应保留论文的科学内容,从而保留其研究质量。
为此,我们设计了一套贯穿重写提示的内容完整性规则(图8-11)。 这些规则规定哪些内容必须保持不变,并要求保留原始文本的长度和结构。
同时,所有重写必须保持语法上和逻辑上

学术 英语,以通过引入语法错误或打字来避免实际降低科学质量.

blocks.en:
Perturbing language proficiency .
Prior work identifies systematic differences between L1 and L2 English
academic writing at the lexical, phraseological, and syntactic levels. Crossley and McNamara (2009) identify differences
in lexical variation and sophistication, while Ädel and Erman (2012) find a larger and more varied repertoire of
recurrent lexical bundles in native English writing. Hinkel (2002) further documents differences across a broader
set of lexical, syntactic, and rhetorical features.
Finally, L1 and L2 writers differ in the linguistic expressions they use to qualify claims and signal certainty, including their choice of words for conveying different degrees of epistemic commitment ( Hyland and Milton, 1997 ) .

blocks.en: 2.2 Rewrite Validation
blocks.zh: 2.2 重写验证

blocks.en:
The validity of our experimental setup depends on two central properties of
the generated rewrites.
First, the rewrite should preserve the scientific content of the original
paper.
Second, the rewriting process should systematically induce the intended
linguistic characteristics.
We therefore evaluate both content integrity and linguistic change for each rewriting dimension.
blocks.zh:
我们实验设置的有效性取决于两个中心属性
生成的重写。
首先,改写应保留原稿的科学内容
纸。
第二,改写过程应系统地引导预期的:
语言特征.
因此,我们评价每个改写内容的完整性和语言变化。

blocks.en:
Validating the content integrity .
First of all, we validate that our systematic rewrites preserve the content integrity of the original paper, and are thus comparable.
To this end, we consider two different measures: semantic similarity and lexical preservation .
Specifically, we compute the semantic similarity between each rewrite and the original paper using dense embeddings. 1 1 1 We use BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 for embedding passages. For long documents, comparing dense embeddings directly can overestimate similarity scores ( Xiao et al., 2023 ) .
Hence, each paper is split into passages, and we then compute the average maximum cosine similarity between original and rewritten passage embeddings.
This ensures that we capture content integrity on a more fine-grained level than with pure paper- or section-level embeddings.
In addition to semantic similarity, we quantify the lexical preservation using cosine similarity between unigram and bigram TF-IDF representations for the original paper and rewrites.
This metric complements semantic similarity and validates whether the technical terminology is preserved.
blocks.zh:
验证内容完整性 .
首先,我们确认,我们系统的改写保留了原始文件的内容完整性,因此具有可比性。
为此,我们考虑了两种不同的措施:语义相似性和词汇保护。
具体来说,我们用稠密的嵌入来计算每个重写和原始纸之间的语义相似性. 1 1,我们使用BAAI/bge-great-en-v1.5来进行嵌入式通道. 对于长文件,比较密集嵌入可直接高估相似分数(Xiao等,2023.
因此,每张纸被分出为段落,然后我们计算出原始和重写段落嵌入之间的平均最大余弦相近性.
这确保了我们在比纯纸或分层嵌入更精细的层次上捕捉内容完整性.
除了语义相近外,我们还利用unigram和bigram TF-IDF代表物之间的相近性对词典保存进行量化,用于原始的纸张和重写.
这一衡量标准补充了语义上的相似性并验证技术术语是否得到保留.

blocks.en:
We report the content-integrity scores in Table 2 .
Across all rewrites, both measures strongly indicate the preservation of scientific content, with scores close to their maximum value of 1 1 .
blocks.zh:
我们在表2中报告内容整合得分。
在所有重写中,这两项措施都强烈表明科学内容的保存,其得分接近其最高值11.

blocks.en:
Validating language proficiency perturbations .
We validate the language-proficiency rewrites using established
measures for lexical and textual complexity.
First, we use Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MTLD) to
measure lexical diversity ( McCarthy and Jarvis, 2010 ) .
This directly reflects our instruction to vary the breadth and
diversity of the vocabulary.
Second, we use Advanced Guiraud (AG) to measure lexical sophistication ( Daller et al., 2003 ) ,
capturing the use of advanced vocabulary.
Both measures are motivated by prior work for identifying systematic differences in lexical variation and sophistication between L1 and L2 English
writing ( Crossley and McNamara, 2009 ) .
Finally, we report the Gunning Fog index (GF) as a broader measure of textual complexity ( Gunning, 1952 ) , which considers sentence length and the prevalence of complex words.
blocks.zh:
验证语言熟练程度扰动 。
我们验证语言能力 重写使用既定的
衡量词汇和文字的复杂性。
首先,我们使用《文字特征多样性测量》
测量词典多样性(McCarthy and Jarvis, 2010.).
这直接反映了我们指示改变宽度
词汇的多样性。
第二,我们使用Advanced Guiraud(AG)来测量词典的复杂程度(Daller等,2003年),
获取高级词汇的使用。
这两项措施的动机都是先前为查明L1和L2英语在词汇差异和精密度方面的系统差异而开展的工作。
(克罗斯利和麦克纳马拉,2009年)
最后,我们报告Gunning Fog指数(GF)是更广泛的文字复杂性的衡量标准(Gunning,1952),它考虑了句子长度和复杂词的流行.

blocks.en:
Table 2 shows the results for this validation step.
The linguistic measures demonstrate the viability of our rewriting prompts for perturbing the language proficiency: all metrics show an increase for native -associated rewrites compared to non-native -associated rewrites.
blocks.zh:
表2显示这一验证步骤的结果。
语言测量表明我们重写诱因干扰语言熟练程度的可行性:所有测量都显示,与非本土重写相比,本土-关联重写增加。

blocks.en:
Validating expressed confidence perturbations .
For expressed confidence, we directly measure the linguistic properties targeted
by our rewriting prompts, and measure the frequency of boosters and hedges per 1000 words.
blocks.zh:
验证表达的信心扰动。
对于表达的信心,我们直接衡量所针对的语言属性
通过我们重写提示 并测量每1000个字的助推器和对冲的频率

blocks.en: As shown in Table 2 , high-confidence rewrites contain substantially more boosters and fewer hedges than low-confidence rewrites, confirming the successful manipulation of expressed confidence.
blocks.zh: 如表2所示,高信心重写包含比低信心重写多得多的助推器和更少的套接器,证实了对表达出的信心的成功操纵.

blocks.en: 2.3 Comparative Reviewing
blocks.zh: 2.3 比较审查

blocks.en:
After systematically rewriting papers and validating the underlying linguistic properties,
we can stress-test LLM reviewers along different linguistic dimensions.
Our framework enables to determine whether papers of the same research quality receive systematically different evaluations based on their linguistic realization.
For each paper and rewriting dimension, the LLM reviewer receives one rewritten version at a time and produces a complete review together with an overall review score.
We then compare the scores assigned to the corresponding versions of the same original paper.
blocks.zh:
在系统重写论文并验证基本语言特性之后,
我们可以用不同语言来测试LLM审查器。
我们的框架能够确定同一份研究质量的论文是否根据其语言的实现而得到系统不同的评价。
对于每篇论文和重写维度,LLM评论员一次收到一个重写版本,并产生完整的评论和总体评论分数.
然后,我们将分配的分数与同一份原始文件的相应版本进行比较。

blocks.en:
Review instructions .
We derive a reviewer prompt from standard reviewing instructions at major AI conferences, including explicit review criteria and guidance on the expected output format.
The specific prompt is provided in Figure 6 .
We conducted preliminary experiments with different prompts and found the LLM reviewers to be largely insensitive to such prompt variations: the direction and significance of all effects remain unchanged
(details in Appendix C ).
blocks.zh:
审查指示
我们从大赦国际主要会议上的标准审查指示,包括明确的审查标准和关于预期产出格式的指导,获得一名审查员。
图6提供了具体的提示。
我们用不同的提示进行了初步实验,发现LLM审查人员对这种迅速变化基本上不敏感:所有影响的方向和意义保持不变。
(详见附录C)。

blocks.en:
Review output .
The reviewer output contains the paper’s strengths,
weaknesses, and suggestions for improvement.
In addition, it includes scores for soundness , significance , evidence , and clarity on a 1–4 scale, a reviewer confidence score on a 1–5 scale, and an overall rating on a 1–10 scale.
We explicitly outline the Likert scale for the overall rating in the prompt to avoid any ambiguities.
blocks.zh:
审查产出。
评论员的产出包含了论文的长处,
弱点,以及改进建议。
此外,它还包括1至4级的稳健性、意义、证据和清晰度的分数、1至5级的评审员信心分和1至10级的总体分数。
我们明确概述了综合评级的Irkrt比额表,以避免任何含糊不清之处。

blocks.en: 2.4 Configuration
blocks.zh: 2.4 配置

blocks.en:
Research papers .
We sample 504 504 research papers from the 2026 reviewing cycle of ICLR, uniformly across the 21 21 primary areas. From each primary area, we randomly sample 12 12 accepted and 12 12 rejected papers.
All papers are anonymized, simulating a double blind peer-review setup.
blocks.zh:
研究论文.
我们抽取了2026年国际海洋研究理事会审查周期的504 504份研究论文,在21个主要领域统一进行。 从每个主要地区,我们随机抽取了12份被接受的文件和12份被拒绝的文件。
所有论文都是匿名的,模拟双盲同行评审设置.

blocks.en:
Rewriting model .
For paper rewriting, we use Claude Opus 5 in all experiments to ensure strong adherence to our prompts.
Keeping the rewriting model fixed prevents differences across reviewers from being confounded by variation in the rewriting model.
blocks.zh:
重写模型 。
对于纸张重写,我们在所有实验中使用克洛德·奥普斯(Claude Opus 5)以确保强烈遵守我们的提示.
保留重写模式可以防止审查者之间的分歧因重写模式的变化而产生混乱。

blocks.en:
LLM reviewers .
For reviewing, we consider LLMs from different model families and capability levels.
We choose only LLMs with a knowledge cutoff before 2026, to avoid any confounding factors due to known acceptance decisions for ICLR 2026.
As proprietary models, we select Gpt-5.5 , Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Gemini 3.5 Flash , as they reflect the default model choices in the respective consumer-facing chat interface as of that cutoff.
In addition, we consider the open-weight models Gemma3 (27B), Qwen3 VL (235B) and Glm4.7 (358B).
blocks.zh:
LLM审查员.
为了审查,我们考虑了来自不同模范家庭和能力级别的法学硕士学位。
我们只选择在2026年之前有知识截断的LLMs,以避免由于已知的ICLR 2026的接受决定而导致任何混淆因素.
作为专有模式,我们选择了Gpt-5.5,克洛德·索内特 4.6和双子座3.5 Flash,因为它们反映了截止时相应的消费者-face聊天界面中的默认模型选择.
此外,我们还考虑开放重量型号为Gemma3(27B),Qune3 VL(235B)和Glm4.7(358B).

blocks.en:
Reviewer variance .
Since LLM-reviewer scores can vary across repeated generations, even for identical inputs, we quantify the reviewer variance for every reviewer-model to help interpret our results.
We randomly sample 10 10 papers and conduct n n = 10 10 independent repeated reviews for each LLM. The variance for each model is reported in Table 3 .
Reviewer variance differs substantially across models: Gpt-5.5 , Claude Sonnet 4.6 , Gemma3 , and Qwen3 VL exhibit pooled standard deviations of approximately 0.5 0.5 rating points, while Glm4.7 ( 0.85 0.85 ) and particularly Gemini 3.5 Flash ( 1.24 1.24 ) show greater variability.
This enables us to contextualize score differences between linguistic rewrites relative to the inherent stochastic variation of the corresponding reviewer.
blocks.zh:
审校差异 .
由于LLM-审查员的分数会因世代相传而异,甚至对于相同的输入,我们量化每个审查员-模型的审查员差异,以帮助解释我们的结果.
我们随机抽取了10篇论文,对每篇LLM进行n=10起独立再审. 每个模型的差异见表3。
各种模型的审阅员差异差别很大:Gpt-5.5,克洛德·索内特 4.6,Gemma3,和Quen3 VL显示集合标准偏差约0.5分,而Glm4.7(0.85 0.85分),特别是双子座3.5 Flash(1.24 1.24分)显示差异较大.
这使得我们能将语言重写者与相应审查者固有的分数差异联系起来。

blocks.en: 3.1 Main Results
blocks.zh: 3.1 主要成果

blocks.en:
We first investigate whether linguistic rewrites
systematically affect the scores assigned by LLM reviewers.
Our primary comparisons are native vs. non-native for language proficiency and high-confidence vs. low-confidence for expressed confidence.
For each pair, we report the percentage of the first version receiving a higher review score, the second version receiving a higher score, or both versions receiving the same score (i.e., a tie).
Table 4 reports our main results.
blocks.zh:
我们首先调查语言是否重写
有系统地影响LLM审查员分配的分数。
我们的主要比较是当地人对语言熟练程度和高度自信的非本地人对表示信心的低信心。
对于每对,我们报告第一个版本获得较高评分的百分比,第二个版本获得较高分数的百分比,或者两个版本都获得相同分数(即平分).
表4报告了我们的主要结果。

blocks.en:
Preferences along the linguistic dimensions .
The first takeaway is that the two linguistic dimensions affect reviewer scores differently.
For the language proficiency dimension, preferences are comparatively weak and inconsistent across reviewers. For 5/6 of the reviewers, native rewrites receive higher scores more often, but the corresponding preference ratios remain subtle (between 1.0 × 1.0\times and 1.3 × 1.3\times ).
In contrast, we observe a consistent and substantially stronger preference towards high-confidence over low-confidence rewrites across all LLM reviewers. High-confidence rewrites are preferred between 1.3 × 1.3\times and 7.0 × 7.0\times as often as their low-confidence counterparts. The most notable preference ratios are observed for Claude Sonnet 4.6 ( 7.0 × 7.0\times ) and Gemma3 ( 6.0 × 6.0\times ).
blocks.zh:
语言方面的偏好
第一种外出方式是两种语言维度对评论员的分数影响不同.
就语言熟练程度而言,各审查者的偏好相对薄弱并不一致。 对5/6的评审者来说,本土重写得分较多,但相应的偏好比率依然微妙(在1.0×1.0相和1.3相和1.3相之间).
相比之下,我们看到,所有LLM审查者都始终更倾向于高度信任而不是低信任重写。 高自信重写在1.3×1.3正时到7.0×7.0正时之间,和他们的低自信对应者一样频繁. 据观察,Claude Sonnet 4.6(7.0×7.0\时)和Gemma3(6.0×6.0\时)的首选比率最为显著。

blocks.en: The average scores show a similar pattern: scores are nearly identical between native and non-native rewrites, but consistently higher for high-confidence than for low-confidence rewrites.
blocks.zh: 平均分数显示类似模式:分数在本土和非本土重写之间几乎相同,但对于高自信的分数始终高于低自信重写.

blocks.en:
Impact on review decisions .

A change in review score becomes more significant as it flips the acceptance decision of the paper. We therefore analyze how frequently our linguistic interventions result in such decision flips. Specifically, we define a decision flip whenever the two rewrites of the same paper fall on opposite sides of the acceptance threshold (4.5 in our case).
Table 4 reports both directions separately: non-native rejection → \rightarrow native acceptance ( First ↑ \uparrow )
and native rejection → \rightarrow non-native acceptance ( Second ↑ \uparrow ),
and for confidence low-confidence rejection → \rightarrow high-confidence acceptance ( First ↑ \uparrow ) and the reverse direction ( Second ↑ \uparrow ).
blocks.zh:
对审查决定的影响

复审分数的改变随着文件的接受决定被推翻而变得更加重要。 因此,我们分析我们的语言干预如何频繁导致这种决定的翻转。 具体地说,当同一文件的两起重写落在接受阈值的两侧时,我们定义了一个决定翻转(我们的情况是4.5)。
表4分别报告两个方向:非本地拒绝 ~ 直截了当的本地接受(第一 ~ )
与本地拒绝 ~ 右侧的非本地接受 (第二 ~ ) ,
而对于信心低落的拒绝 ~\右倾的高度信心接受(第一 \\ ) 和反向(第二 \ \ )

blocks.en:
For language proficiency, decision flips are largely balanced, which is consistent with the absence of a systematic score preference.
For confidence, flips predominantly favor the high-confidence version.
We observe the most drastic effect for Claude Sonnet 4.6 : in 21.0 % 21.0\% of reviews, Claude Sonnet 4.6 accepts the high-confidence version and reject the low-confidence version, with only 2.8 % 2.8\% of papers accepted only for the low-confidence rewrite.
As the average scores for Gemma3 and Qwen3 VL lie well above the acceptance threshold, decision flips are rare for these models.
blocks.zh:
对于语言熟练程度,决定翻转基本平衡,这与没有系统分数偏好是一致的.
对于信心,翻转主要倾向于高自信版本.
我们观察到对克洛德·索内特4.6最强烈的影响:在21.0%的评语中克洛德·索内特4.6接受高自信版本并拒绝低自信版本,只有2.8% 2.8%的论文只接受低自信重写.
由于Gemma3和Qwen3 VL的平均分数远远高于接受阈值,这些模型很少出现决定翻转.

blocks.en: 3.2 In-depth Analysis
blocks.zh: 3.2 深入分析

blocks.en:
Combined effects of linguistic style .

Our main experiments consider language proficiency and confidence in isolation.
This analysis investigates how both dimensions interact when they occur simultaneously.
For a batch of 126 papers, we generate four additional rewrites,
including all combinations of the two dimensions.
The corresponding rewriting prompts are merged (see Figures 12 - 15 in the Appendix).
We then investigate
(i) the language proficiency dimension given a specific confidence rewrite,
(ii) the confidence dimension given a specific proficiency rewrite,
(iii) the comparison of the two extremes ( native & high-confidence vs. non-native & low-confidence ),
and (iv) the inverse ( native & low-confidence vs. non-native & high-confidence ).
Table 5 shows the results of this analysis.
blocks.zh:
语言风格的综合效应 .

我们的主要实验考虑语言熟练程度和对孤立的信心.
这一分析研究了两个维度同时发生时的相互作用.
对于一批126份论文,我们产生4个额外的重写,
包括两个维度的所有组合。
相应的重写提示被合并(见附录图12至图15)。
然后我们调查
(一) 语言熟练程度方面的具体信心重写,
(二) 重写特定熟练程度的信心方面,
(三) 两个极端的比较(本土和高自信与非本土和低自信),
(四) 反向(原生和低自信与非生和高自信)。
表5显示了这一分析的结果。

blocks.en:
The conditional comparisons largely reproduce the effects observed when varying the dimensions in isolation. Holding confidence fixed, differences between native and non-native rewrites are slightly more pronounced but remain relatively small.
The preference for high-confidence rewrites persists when combined with the proficiency dimension.
The cross-condition comparisons further illustrate the strength of the confidence effect.
When native and high-confidence language are combined and compared against non-native & low-confidence rewrites, the former is preferred with preference ratios of up to 9.1 × 9.1\times .
Reversing the confidence dimension switches this pattern, with all reviewers favoring
the non-native but high-confidence rewrite.
Across the board, the confidence dimension dominates these combined comparisons.
blocks.zh:
有条件的比较基本上重复了孤立地改变维度时观察到的效果。 原生和非原生重写之间保持了一定的信心,其差异略为明显,但仍相对较小。
在与熟练程度相结合时,仍然倾向于重写高自信。
交叉条件比较进一步说明了信心效应的强度.
当将本地语言和高自信语言合并起来,与非本地语言和低自信重写相比时,前者更受青睐,首选比例可达9.1×9.1\时.
倒置信心维度开关此模式,所有审查者都赞成
非本土但高自信重写。
总体而言,信心层面主导这些综合比较。

blocks.en:
Preferences along the language proficiency dimension .

Our main results discover substantial effects of linguistic rewrites along the confidence dimension,
but only subtle changes along the proficiency dimension.
A natural question that arises is whether LLM reviewers are indeed not substantially affected by language proficiency, or whether our rewrites are not sufficient for bringing out existing biases (despite validated rewriting effects by linguistic metrics; see Table 2 ).
To answer this question, we simulate biased reviewers by injecting a dedicated instruction into the reviewer prompt:
“ In addition to assessing the scientific content, place substantial weight on the linguistic style and overall presentation of the paper … ”
(full prompt in Figure 7 ).
We intentionally keep the prompt general, and avoid mentioning language proficiency directly.
We run this analysis on 126 papers, equally drawn from the primary areas (see Table 9 in the Appendix for the full results).

Aspects that drive the reviews .

Review scores alone do not decide the outcome of the peer review process. Arguments brought up in the review are also decisive in deriving an acceptance decision ( Arous et al., 2026 ) .
We therefore extend our study beyond the plain review scores, and investigate which aspects of a paper ( Lu et al., 2025 ) drive the reviewers’ assessments and whether this focus changes with linguistic style.
In particular, we study whether linguistic variations affect the attention
given to the underlying scientific content.

blocks.en: 4 Related Work
blocks.zh: 4 相关工作

blocks.en:
LLMs for peer review .
With increasing paper submissions, conferences and reviewers have explored the use of LLMs to assist with peer review ( Jin et al., 2024 ; Demetrio et al., 2025 ; Thakkar et al., 2026 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ; Huang et al., 2025 ) . While promising, LLM-based reviewing raises reliability and fairness concerns, including biases toward author-related properties such as affiliation, seniority, and publication history ( Ye et al., 2024 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ; Vasu et al., 2026 ) , as well as sensitivity to textual adversarial attacks and prompt injections. Most closely related, Kousha and Thelwall (2026) find that linguistic complexity and text length are more strongly associated with ChatGPT-based research evaluations than with expert-based evaluations in many fields. We complement this work by applying controlled, linguistically grounded transformations to the same papers, manipulating language proficiency and expressed confidence while preserving research content. This isolates effects of linguistic presentation from differences across papers.
blocks.zh:
同行审查的法学硕士。
随着越来越多的文件提交,会议和审查人员已探索利用有限责任公司协助同行审评(Jin等,2024;Demetrio等,2025;Thakkar等,2026;Zhu等,2025;Huang等,2025)。 以LLM为基础的审查虽然很有希望,但引起了可靠性和公正性问题,包括对作者相关财产的偏见,如归属、资历和出版历史(Ye等,2024;Zhu等,2025;Vasu等,2026),以及对文字对抗攻击和即时注射的敏感性。 最密切相关的是克沙和特尔沃尔(2026年)发现语言复杂性和文本长度与基于ChatGPT的研究评价相比,在许多领域与基于专家的评价更紧密地联系在一起. 我们通过对同一篇论文进行有控制的、基于语言的转换、操纵语言熟练程度和在保留研究内容的同时表示信心来补充这项工作。 这把语言表述的效果与不同论文的差异隔离开来.

blocks.en:
Linguistic biases in human peer review .
Prior linguistic research documents systematic differences between L1 and L2 English writing. Crossley and McNamara (2009) identify differences in lexical variation and sophistication, while Ädel and Erman (2012) find that native English writers employ a larger and more varied repertoire of recurrent lexical bundles. Differences also extend to epistemic expression: Hyland and Milton (1997) show that L1 and L2 writers differ in the range and precision with which they express qualification and certainty. Linguistic presentation can also affect human peer review. In a controlled experiment, Politzer-Ahles et al. (2020) find preliminary evidence that identical scientific content receives lower ratings when presented in non-native-like rather than native-like English, although the manual interventions limited the study to paper abstracts. Similarly, an observational study of submissions to Stroke finds lower priority scores and acceptance rates for submissions from non-English-speaking countries, even after controlling for potential confounders ( Saposnik et al., 2014 ) . Beyond language proficiency, Sayegh et al. (2024) find a modest association between writing style and publication recommendations in a simulated peer-review experiment. These findings motivate our controlled investigation of whether linguistic presentation similarly affects LLM-based peer review, particularly given evidence of linguistic biases in other LLM applications ( Hofmann et al., 2024 ; Reusens et al., 2025 ; Deas et al., 2023 ) .
blocks.zh:
人类同行审查中的语言偏见
先前的语言研究记录了L1和L2英语写作的系统差异. Crossley和McNamara(2009年)查明了词汇变化和精密程度的差异,而Ädel和Erman(2012年)则发现,英国本土作家使用的是更大更多样化的反复出现的词汇包。 差异还延伸到了感官表达:Hyland和Milton(1997年)表明,L1和L2作家在表达资格和确定性的范围和精确度上有所不同. 语言表述也可能影响人类同行审查。 在受控实验中,Politzer-Ahles等人(2020年)发现初步证据表明,相同的科学内容在以非本土性而非本土性英语呈现时获得较低的评价,尽管人工干预将研究局限于纸质摘要. 同样,对向Stroke提交划界案的观察研究发现,非英语国家提交的划界案的优先得分和接受率较低,甚至在控制潜在混乱者之后也是如此(Saposnik等,2014年)。 除了语言能力,Sayegh等人(2024年)在模拟同行评审实验中发现写作风格与出版建议之间有适度的联系. 这些调查结果促使我们对语言表达是否同样影响基于LLM的同行审评进行有控制的调查,特别是鉴于其他LLM应用中存在语言偏差的证据(Hofmann等,2024;Reusens等,2025;Deas等,2023)。

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
In this work, we propose a controlled framework for investigating linguistic biases in LLM-based peer review.
Our framework applies interventions to research papers along linguistic markers of epistemic authority, while preserving the underlying scientific content.
Our experiments reveal substantial preferences of LLM reviewers toward rewrites using high-confidence language.
Crucially, these preferences frequently result in decision flips across the accept ↔ \leftrightarrow reject boundary, directly affecting review outcomes.
Beyond scores, we find that aspects raised in reviews vary in frequency and sentiment depending on linguistic features of the paper, potentially influencing final decisions.
blocks.zh:
在这项工作中,我们提议在基于LLM的同行审评中建立一个调查语言偏见的控制框架。
我们的框架在保留基本科学内容的同时,按照流行病学权威的语言标志对研究论文采取干预措施。
我们的实验揭示了LLM审查员对使用高自信语言改写的强烈偏好.
关键是,这些偏好往往导致决定翻转,跨越接受的\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\“拒绝界限,直接影响到审查的结果。
除了评分之外,我们发现,审查中提出的方面在频率和情绪上因文件的语言特点而异,有可能影响最后决定。

blocks.en:
Our findings raise important concerns for the use of LLMs in peer review.
If content-equivalent papers receive different scores and review arguments solely because of linguistic properties, reviewer judgments do not exclusively reflect scientific quality.
LLM reviewers should therefore be stress-tested on content-preserving rewrites to determine whether linguistic changes systematically affect their assessments.
These tests should cover multiple linguistic dimensions and examine both overall scores and review arguments.
In particular, reviewer systems should be checked for whether expressed confidence is treated as a signal of stronger evidence or scientific quality.
Our framework enables these tests and comparisons of reviewer configurations by the stability of their assessments under controlled linguistic interventions.
Finally, substantial differences in average scores and within-model variance caution against treating raw scores from individual LLM reviewers as directly comparable without calibration.
Future work can extend these stress tests to additional linguistic and rhetorical dimensions.
blocks.zh:
我们的调查结果引起了对在同行审议中使用法学硕士的重要关切。
如果内容等同的论文仅仅因为语言特性而得到不同的分数和审查论据,评论员的判断并不完全反映科学质量.
因此,LLM审查员应接受内容保留重写的压力测试,以确定语言变化是否系统地影响其评估。
这些测试应涵盖多种语言层面,并审查总分和审查论点。
特别是,应检查审查员制度是否将表示的信心视为更强有力的证据或科学质量的信号。
我们的框架通过在受控制的语言干预下评估的稳定性,使这些测试和审查者配置比较成为可能。
最后,在平均分和模型内差异方面有重大差异,告诫不要将个别LLM审查员的原始分数视为直接可比而不加校正。
今后的工作可以将这些压力测试扩大到其他语言和修辞层面。

blocks.en: Ethics statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en: This work does not advocate the use of LLMs as replacements for human peer reviewers. Instead, we develop a controlled framework to identify and characterize biases in LLM-based reviewing. Our study shows that linguistic properties of a paper can affect LLM-generated review outcomes even when the underlying research content is preserved. Such sensitivity raises fairness concerns, as linguistic variation associated with researchers’ backgrounds may influence how their work is evaluated.
blocks.zh: 这项工作不提倡使用法学硕士作为人类同行审评员的替代。 相反,我们制定了控制框架,以查明并描述基于LLM的审查中的偏差。 我们的研究表明,即使保存了基础研究内容,论文的语言特性也会影响LLM产生的审查结果. 这种敏感性引起了公平问题,因为与研究人员背景有关的语言差异可能影响对其工作的评价。

blocks.en: Our findings also have potential for dual use. Identifying linguistic features that systematically influence LLM reviewers could be used to deliberately manipulate papers in order to obtain more favorable automated reviews. We do not intend to facilitate such manipulation. Rather, we use these findings to expose potential vulnerabilities of LLM-based reviewing and to motivate their careful evaluation before such systems are used in high-stakes peer-review settings.
blocks.zh: 我们的调查结果还有可能具有双重用途。 确定有系统地影响LLM审查者的语言特征可以被用来故意操纵论文,以便获得更有利的自动审查。 我们不打算为这种操纵提供便利。 相反,我们利用这些调查结果来揭露基于LLM的审查的潜在弱点,并激励它们进行认真评估,然后再将这些系统用于高水平的同行审查。

blocks.en: Confidence Indicators . To quantify expressed confidence, we measure the use of boosters (e.g., “clearly,” “demonstrates,” “certainly”) and hedges (e.g., “may” “suggests”, “likely”) drawn from Hyland’s metadiscourse taxonomy ( Hyland, 2005 ) . Each paper was segmented into chunks, normalized (lowercased, punctuation-stripped), and scanned for booster and hedge terms using word-boundary-anchored matching (“\b” in regular expressions) to ensure only whole-word occurrences were counted. We report frequency per 1,000 words for each category, with booster and hedge terms kept mutually exclusive to avoid double-counting.

blocks.en:
Magnitude of score differences .
The preferences we identify are driven by consistent shifts across many
papers rather than by a few extreme score changes.
For the overall rating, 88% of native / non-native pairs and 85% of high-confidence / low-confidence pairs differ by at most one point, and on the
review criteria (scored on a 1–4 scale) fewer than 4% of pairs differ by
two or more points.
The confidence effects in Table 4 therefore
reflect a systematic, directional shift in how reviewers assess the same
paper, rather than occasional outliers.
Larger differences of two or more points concentrate on Gemini 3.5 Flash and Glm4.7 (28–37% of pairs, compared to at most 9% for all other
reviewers), the two reviewers with the highest variance across repeated
generations (Table 3 ).
Our framework cleanly separates this stochastic variation from genuine
rewrite effects: the mean absolute score difference of these reviewers is
nearly identical for both rewrite dimensions (1.20 vs. 1.23 for Gemini 3.5 Flash , 1.29 vs. 1.36 for Glm4.7 ), yet only the confidence
rewrites induce a systematic preference.
Comparing paired rewrites of the same paper thus reveals stylistic biases
even for reviewers whose individual scores fluctuate considerably.
